newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen to firm with crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen to firm with crude gains.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were expected to edge higher from Tuesday on firm crude prices, traders said.
On Tuesday, 180-centistoke fuel oil for loading in October were indicated between $120-$122 per tonne.
Traders said prices would continue to draw support from strong crude prices but cash supplies were adequate to meet demand.
One tradersaid distressed supplies from South Korea were offered at a slight discount to Singapore spot quotes. He said inventories remained high in Singapore.
Chinese buyers were sidelined by current high prices while some have already covered their October requirements earlier this month.
In the swaps market, October fuel oil was discussed at $120.25/$121.50, slightly over Tuesday's $120/$122.
